segments.say: Lesson 18. Design a News Feed (Instagram / X). Fan-out on write versus read, the celebrity problem, hybrid feeds, ranking and feed caches.

Design a social feed like Instagram or X: when you open the app, show recent posts from people you follow, ranked, in milliseconds. Here is an analogy. A newspaper delivery service: for most readers, papers are pre-packed overnight (fan-out on write); for papers with millions of readers, you collect them at the counter when you arrive (fan-out on read).

Why does this matter? Classic trade-off question: push versus pull, and the celebrity problem. A few key words. Fan-out on write: Push new posts into followers' feeds immediately. Fan-out on read: Build the feed when the user opens it. Celebrity problem: Accounts with millions of followers. Hydration: Turning post I Ds into full post data.

segments.say: Fan-out on write versus read. Priya (500 followers) posts a photo.

segments.sec: Watch: Fan-out on write vs read
segments.say: Fan-out on write (push): immediately insert the post I D into each follower's precomputed feed cache (Redis list). Reads become a single fast lookup.

segments.sec: Watch: Fan-out on write vs read
segments.say: But a celebrity with 80M followers would mean 80M writes per post: slow, wasteful, a hot spot. That's the celebrity problem.

segments.sec: Watch: Fan-out on write vs read
segments.say: Fan-out on read (pull) for celebrities: don't push. At read time fetch their recent posts and merge.

segments.sec: Watch: Fan-out on write vs read
segments.say: Hybrid: push for normal users, pull for celebrities, merged and ranked (recency, affinity, engagement) when the user opens the app.

Core components. Post service: stores posts (sharded D B) and media in object storage plus C D N. Social graph service: who follows whom (graph D B or sharded adjacency tables). Fan-out workers: consume "PostCreated" from Kafka, write to follower feed caches. Feed service: reads feed cache (post I Ds), hydrates post and user details from caches, ranks, paginates with cursors. Ranking: starts chronological; M L ranking uses features like affinity, engagement and freshness.

Details that impress. Store only post I Ds in feeds (small) and keep the most recent ~500–1000. Skip fan-out to inactive users and compute their feeds on demand. Counts (likes/views) are eventually consistent, batched counters. Deleted or edited posts: filter at hydration time.

Say it in the interview. "It's extremely read-heavy, so I precompute feeds with fan-out on write via Kafka workers into Redis feed lists of post I Ds, except for high-follower accounts, which are pulled and merged at read time: a hybrid model. The feed service hydrates I Ds from caches, ranks and paginates with cursors. Media is served from C D N, and counters are eventually consistent.".

Let's compare. Read latency: very fast, slower (gather plus merge). Write cost: high ( times followers), low. Celebrity: explosion, fine. Inactive users: wasted work, no waste. Freshness: instant, computed on read.

A likely interview question: Push versus pull feeds? A strong answer: Push precomputes feeds on write for fast reads but explodes for celebrities. Pull computes at read time, cheap writes but slow reads. Hybrid: push for regular users, pull and merge for celebrities.
That's it for Design a News Feed (Instagram / X). Now play the quiz and games in the app to lock it in. See you in the next lesson.
